evidence_items.publisher: Core Scientific (via Business Wire, republished by Silicon UK)
evidence_items.locator: section Fiscal Year 2024 Financial Results, paragraph 1

receipt.public_excerpt: Total revenue for the year ended December 31, 2024 was $510.7 million, consisting of $408.7 million in digital asset self-mining revenue, $77.6 million in digital asset hosted mining revenue and $24.4 million in HPC hosting revenue.

evidence_items.explanation: HPC hosting was under 5% of 2024 revenue; bitcoin mining was the rest. This supports the gist that operating AI/HPC capacity was small relative to the headline deal.

evidence_items.publisher: roic.ai (transcript of Core Scientific Q4 2024 earnings call)

receipt.public_excerpt: we generated $8.5 million in HPC hosting revenue during the quarter and, as expected, exited the year with 16.5 megawatts of critical IT load

evidence_items.explanation: Before the post, Core Scientific publicly reported a specific operating HPC footprint of 16.5 MW that was earning revenue. That is documented capacity, which cuts against 'little proof... at all', though it is about 3% of the 500+ MW deal.

evidence_items.publisher: roic.ai (transcript of Core Scientific Q4 2024 earnings call)
evidence_items.locator: Q&A, answer to Brett Knoblauch (Cantor Fitzgerald)

receipt.public_excerpt: That number does include the 16.5 megawatts.

evidence_items.explanation: The CEO confirmed that the 250 MW year-end 2025 target includes the 16.5 MW already running. Most of the capacity was still to be built when Zitron wrote.

unresolved_gaps: Could not read the FY2024 10-K or the earnings slides directly (SEC returned 403), so capacity figures come from the call transcript.
'Meaningful' has no stated threshold, so whether 16.5 MW counts is a judgment call.
